The test image shows soybean leaves with distinct white, powdery patches on the upper leaf surfaces. This is a leaf disease. The white powdery coating strongly suggests **Powdery_Mildew**, but let me verify by checking references across candidates.

Let me view references from my top candidates, one at a time.
Strong match - white powdery patches on leaves. Let me check Downy_mildew next.
Downy mildew shows yellow spots, not white powdery coating. Clearly different from the test image. Let me check Bacterial_Pustule.
Bacterial Pustule shows small brown spots with raised centers, not white powdery patches. Not a match. Let me check Frogeye_leaf_spot.
Frogeye leaf spot shows gray spots with reddish-brown borders and holes. Not a match. Let me check Cercospora.
Cercospora shows reddish-purple/bronze discoloration with necrotic spots. Not a match. Let me check Soybean_rust.
Soybean rust shows small tan/brown spots. Not a match. Let me check Phyllosticta_leaf_spot.
Phyllosticta shows tan/brown lesions with purplish margins. Not a match. Let me view one more Powdery Mildew reference to confirm.

This confirms it. Both Powdery Mildew references show the same white, powdery coating on leaf surfaces that matches the test image perfectly. The test image shows:

- White, powdery patches scattered across multiple soybean leaves
- Patches coalescing on some leaves to cover larger areas
- Upper leaf surface affected
- No brown/necrotic lesions, no yellow spots, no holes

This matches the Powdery Mildew description exactly: "White, powdery coating on leaves that begins as small patches and coalesces to cover entire leaves."

All other candidates checked (Downy mildew, Bacterial Pustule, Frogeye leaf spot, Cercospora, Soybean rust, Phyllosticta leaf spot) show distinctly different symptom patterns (spots, lesions, discoloration) rather than the white powdery coating seen here.
